outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the problem has had two partial results (Kc and Soto Levins, April 2024, positivity for Serre liftable modules over some ramified rings; Bhatt, Hochster and Ma, October 2024, equal-characteristic positivity and a mixed-characteristic result conditional on lim Cohen-Macaulay sequences) and, on 6 October 2026, a full-scope claim in an OpenAI preprint ('Positivity of Serre's Intersection Multiplicity', dated 23 September 2026) that the sources describe as covering the ramified mixed-characteristic case; as of 13 October 2026 I found no Lean proof of that claim, no named expert engagement with its argument, and I could not read the preprint text itself.
problem_asks: (1) Let R be any commutative regular local ring (no restriction on characteristic or ramification). (2) Let P and Q be any prime ideals of R. (3) Suppose dim(R/P) + dim(R/Q) = dim R. (4) Then the Serre intersection multiplicity chi(R/P, R/Q) is strictly positive. Implicit in (4): chi is defined only when R/P tensor R/Q has finite length. The Wikipedia wording does not state this hypothesis; the DeepMind formal-conjectures Lean version does (IsFiniteLength). The bullet asks only for the quotient form (R/P, R/Q). Serre's original module form (chi(M,N) > 0 for finitely generated M, N with finite-length tensor product and dim M + dim N = dim R) is more general and is the form the OpenAI claim is reported to prove. The bullet asks for no bound, no range of dimensions, and no counterexample.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's openai/math release (made public 6 October 2026; the README gives 719 manuscripts in 372 families, press coverage says 722) includes a preprint titled 'Positivity of Serre's Intersection Multiplicity'. Its folder is preprints/Positivity-of-Serres-Intersection-Multiplicity-September-23-2026 (commit adc7f1241b42), its author line reads 'Author: OpenAI', and its date is 'September 23, 2026' (31 pages, Apache-2.0). Per the formal-conjectures issue #6911 and the unaoya/SerrePositivity README, the preprint claims a proof of Serre's positivity conjecture 'in full, including ramified mixed characteristic' for nonzero finitely generated modules M, N over a regular local ring with finite-length tensor product and dim M + dim N = dim R; the quotient case R/P, R/Q is a special case. The family number 193 comes from the unaoya SOURCE.md; the family page was not reachable. The Valency aggregator lists an OpenAI entry titled 'Positivity of Serre's Intersection Multiplicity' (ID W_zaj9g542). I could not read the PDF (WebFetch returned compressed PDF bytes and local PDF tooling was not approved), so the claim's wording above is second-hand.
events.revisions: Dated 23 Sep 2026 on the paper and its folder; first public appearance I could find is the 6 Oct 2026 release (unaoya SOURCE.md records retrieval at commit adc7f124 on 2026-10-06). No later version of this paper found. Three other manuscripts (Hodge-conjecture-related, not Serre) were withdrawn on 7 Oct 2026 for a sign error, and fourteen received proof repairs; I found no indication that this paper was among them, but I did not read the full repository history.
events.delivers: Claimed (not independently checked): for a regular local ring (R, m) and nonzero finitely generated R-modules M, N with finite-length M tensor N and dim M + dim N = dim R, chi(M, N) > 0, including ramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic; specialising to M = R/P, N = R/Q gives chi(R/P, R/Q) > 0 for all primes P, Q with dim R/P + dim R/Q = dim R (per the issue and README descriptions). I have not confirmed the paper's own theorem statement, hypotheses, or whether its argument uses any conditional input.
events.remains: If the claim holds, nothing of the problem remains open. On the evidence I could read, nothing has been independently established: no Lean proof exists upstream for this paper, and the third-party Lean project has only a sorry-proved statement skeleton (Theorem 1.1 and a core case).
events.time_since_posted: 7 days as of 13 Oct 2026. No named commutative algebraist has publicly engaged with the argument in the sources I could reach. GitHub activity is a status proposal (formal-conjectures #6911, no replies) and a statement-level Lean skeleton (unaoya). The Institute for Advanced Study advisory group's statement, as reported in press coverage I did not open directly, says the group's role is not an endorsement of any result.

events.doubts: (1) No Lean proof from OpenAI for this paper (issue #6911); OpenAI's own README says not all results have Lean formalizations, that about 42% of top-line results are formalized, and that 'some of the unformalized results could have issues'. (2) The only formal work is a third-party skeleton; its README says the first milestone, a sorry-free derivation of Theorem 1.1, is still a target, and it places the claim as an unproven statement ('証明なしの主張として置く' in Statement.lean). (3) No named expert has written on the argument within 7 days. (4) The same release has already had a withdrawal for a sign error (Hodge-related manuscripts). (5) The scope and method are second-hand; I could not check the hypotheses, whether the argument uses any conditional input, or whether it handles every ramified mixed-characteristic ring. (6) Context for weighing rather than doubt: Bhatt, Hochster and Ma (2024, v2 Aug 2026) identify the mixed-characteristic positivity case as reducing to lim Cohen-Macaulay sequences, which they do not establish for ramified rings, and the Wikipedia article (last edited 24 Aug 2026, before this claim) still says the general case is open. How the OpenAI argument avoids that route is not described in any source I could read.
events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction: asserts strict positivity chi > 0 whenever dim M + dim N = dim R and the tensor product has finite length, in all regular local rings including the ramified mixed-characteristic case that the earlier literature listed as the open one.

events.what_happened: Bhargav Bhatt, Melvin Hochster and Linquan Ma, 'Lim Cohen-Macaulay sequences of modules' (arXiv:2410.18372). Introduces lim Cohen-Macaulay sequences of modules and proves they exist for F-finite local rings of prime characteristic (Theorem 5.4). The introduction (v1 and v2) states that 'one consequence of our results is a proof that the Serre multiplicity behaves correctly in the equal characteristic case', with equal characteristic 0 following by reduction to prime characteristic p > 0. For mixed characteristic, Theorem 6.1 is conditional: if R := T/P and S := T/Q (T regular local) have lim Cohen-Macaulay sequences, then chi(R, S) > 0; Corollary 6.3 gives the dimension-bounded consequence for complete local domains with perfect or algebraically closed residue field, conditional on the existence of such sequences there. The v2 abstract says that existence in mixed characteristic 'would imply' the long-open conjecture on positivity of Serre intersection multiplicities for all regular local rings, and that the paper proves existence only for certain mixed-characteristic rings.
events.revisions: v1 submitted 24 Oct 2024 (62 KB); v2 submitted 25 Aug 2026 (63 KB, comment '56 pages, final version'). The v1 HTML uses a stronger definition of lim Cohen-Macaulay sequence than the final version, per a search summary of Hochster's final PDF. Journal: Journal fur die reine und angewandte Mathematik (Crelle), vol. 835 (2026), pp. 111-169, DOI 10.1515/crelle-2026-0021, reported in a search summary only (the publisher page refused fetches).
events.delivers: Equal characteristic: positivity of Serre's chi for regular local rings containing a field (char p directly; char 0 by reduction), per the v1 and v2 introductions. Mixed characteristic: conditional only, on existence of lim Cohen-Macaulay sequences for the relevant complete local domains; the ramified mixed-characteristic case, which the bullet's general statement covers, is not settled unconditionally by this paper. Note: the equal-characteristic case was already covered by pre-window results per secondary summaries (Kurano-Roberts; Kc-Soto Levins intro, which says positivity is stated for unramified rings, equal characteristic or mixed (0,p)), so this equal-characteristic claim may overlap known cases; I did not resolve that.
events.remains: The ramified mixed-characteristic case of positivity for all regular local rings, unless lim Cohen-Macaulay sequences exist there. v2 section 1.6 says the remaining ramified case 'remains open in all dimensions >= 5' (quoted via a summarising fetch; the dimension <= 4 situation is attributed to an older Hochster reference).

events.doubts: No specific error identified in any source I read. Points to weigh: (a) the equal-characteristic claim may overlap earlier results (see delivers); (b) the mixed-characteristic statement is conditional and the authors say existence results are 'very limited in mixed characteristic'; (c) the search summary describes a 2025 paper (Ishiro-Shimomoto, arXiv:2509.06527) as restating the Serre conjecture under lim CM sequences, but the abstract page I opened for that paper does not mention Serre positivity, so that claim is unresolved; (d) v1 used a stronger definition of lim Cohen-Macaulay sequence than v2.

events.what_happened: Nawaj KC and Andrew J. Soto Levins, 'On liftings of modules of finite projective dimension' (arXiv:2404.17572). Defines Serre liftable modules (modules that lift to a regular local ring so that Serre's dimension inequality becomes an equality) and proves Serre's positivity for them: when one module M is Serre liftable, finite length of M tensor N and dim M + dim N = dim R give chi(M, N) > 0. The introduction says 'it suffices to assume M is Serre liftable'. The abstract says the result gives 'new cases of Serre's positivity conjecture over ramified regular local rings'; the body says 'Positivity remains an open conjecture for ramified regular local rings'. The paper also gives a length bound (Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity) and special cases of the Iyengar-Ma-Walker length conjecture, which are different questions.
events.revisions: v1 submitted 26 Apr 2024 (the earlier term was 'Dimly liftable'); v2 submitted 5 Nov 2024, which renamed the notion 'Serre liftable' after referee suggestions and is described as forthcoming in IMRN. A bibliographic record (EBSCO, search snippet, not opened) lists IMRN 2024, no. 24.
events.delivers: Positivity for pairs of finitely generated modules over regular local rings in which one module (M) is Serre liftable, under finite length of M tensor N and dim M + dim N = dim R. Covers some ramified rings for that module class. I did not establish that R/P and R/Q are Serre liftable in general, so the quotient form of the bullet is not covered in general by this paper.
events.remains: Positivity for ramified regular local rings in general, i.e. pairs in which neither module is Serre liftable; and the general quotient-form statement for all primes P, Q.

checked_by.what_they_did: Referee suggestions prompted the v2 revision (renaming and substantial revisions per the arXiv comments); publication in IMRN stated as forthcoming on arXiv and listed in an EBSCO record (not opened)

The abstract does not mention Serre's positivity conjecture, intersection multiplicities, or ramified rings.

Presumably an exposition of Gabber's nonnegativity theorem in the ramified case. I could not open it: WebFetch returned compressed PDF bytes, and the title and date come from the search result only.

events.what_happened: Dutta (2008), per the Wikipedia article on Serre's multiplicity conjectures: proves positivity when the projective scheme of a graded ring is artinian local and one module has a finite resolution by direct sums of O(t). Dutta's lecture notes (Utah) are cited as a source; I did not open them.
events.delivers: Positivity in a restricted graded setting (projective scheme artinian local; one module with a finite resolution by sums of O(t)). Not a general statement for regular local rings.
events.remains: Positivity for general regular local rings, including the cases the bullet covers.
events.direction: In the conjectured direction, for a restricted graded class.

events.what_happened: Chris Skalit, 'Positivity of Intersection Multiplicity Over a Two-Dimensional Base' (arXiv:1510.05146, v1 17 Oct 2015). Proves positivity when the regular local ring is essentially smooth over a two-dimensional regular base (the abstract's key clause is that Serre's intersection multiplicity conjecture 'holds for a formal power series ring A'). States that the general case of positivity 'still remains open'. Uses the result for a transversality theorem in the unramified case. Wikipedia cites Skalit (2019); the journal is given as JPAA, 'to appear'.
events.delivers: Positivity for regular local rings essentially smooth over a two-dimensional regular base (including formal power series rings over such a base, per the abstract).
events.remains: Positivity for regular local rings outside that class, including the ramified mixed-characteristic case in general.
events.time_since_posted: about 11 years. I found no independent verification in my searches; Wikipedia cites the result.
events.direction: In the conjectured direction, for a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Serre's original results (Algebre locale, 1965, as cited by secondary sources): for equal-characteristic regular local rings and unramified mixed-characteristic rings, Serre established the dimension inequality and the other parts of the conjecture, and the positivity and nonnegativity in these cases. The ramified mixed-characteristic case was left open. I did not open Serre's book or a primary text; this rests on summaries in the Kurano-Roberts and Kyoto RIMS material and in the Kc-Soto Levins introduction.
events.delivers: Positivity for equal-characteristic and unramified mixed-characteristic regular local rings (secondary-source statement). The Wikipedia article does not state this; the DeepMind formal-conjectures Lean file tags these special cases as solved (per a summarising fetch).
events.remains: The ramified mixed-characteristic case, and the general quotient-form statement for ramified rings.
events.doubts: Scope of Serre's result as summarised is secondary; I did not verify whether it covers all equal-characteristic rings or only the power-series form. The Kurano-Roberts summary says the positivity known in these cases is for the power-series completion.
events.direction: In the conjectured direction, for equal-characteristic and unramified mixed-characteristic rings.

events.what_happened: Paul Roberts (1985, local Chern characters) and independently Gillet and Soule (1987, K-theory) proved the vanishing part of Serre's conjecture: chi(R/P, R/Q) = 0 when dim R/P + dim R/Q < dim R. Dutta gave a new proof in 2008 (Wikipedia). I did not open the primary papers.
events.delivers: Vanishing when the dimensions sum to less than dim R. This is a different part of Serre's conjecture, not the strict positivity the bullet asks for.
events.remains: Strict positivity when the dimensions sum to exactly dim R (the bullet's question).
events.direction: Vanishing (conjectured direction for a different part of the conjecture); discounted for the positivity question.

events.what_happened: Ofer Gabber proved the nonnegativity part of Serre's conjecture (chi >= 0 for all regular local rings) using de Jong's regular alterations, presented in a 1995 talk; the result was never published by Gabber, and accounts appear in Berthelot's Bourbaki expose and in Hochster's notes (Wikipedia; search summaries). I did not open these accounts.
events.delivers: Nonnegativity (part (a)) for all regular local rings. Not positivity.
events.remains: Strict positivity, which is the bullet's question.
events.doubts: The result is unpublished by its author; accounts by others are the only written record I found.
events.direction: In the conjectured direction, for a different part of the conjecture (nonnegativity); discounted for the positivity question.

disputes.summary: DeepMind formal-conjectures issue #6911 proposes marking the two positivity declarations research solved on the strength of the OpenAI preprint, while the Lean file at commit 96119ca3 still tags them research open; no maintainer reply is posted.

Whether the Bhatt-Hochster-Ma equal-characteristic positivity statement is new: pre-window secondary summaries say Serre's results already cover equal-characteristic and unramified cases, so the BHM equal-characteristic claim may re-prove known cases. Not resolved here.

summary: Search and reading covered the arXiv preprints for the in-window partial results, the OpenAI release and its catalogue and README, the DeepMind formal-conjectures issue and Lean file, the third-party Lean project (unaoya/SerrePositivity), the Wikipedia article on Serre's multiplicity conjectures (last edited 24 Aug 2026, before the OpenAI claim), and secondary press and aggregator coverage. Two in-window results are partial. Kc and Soto Levins (arXiv 26 Apr 2024, v2 5 Nov 2024; described as forthcoming in IMRN) prove positivity when one module is Serre liftable, which covers some ramified rings; their abstract says 'new cases ... over ramified regular local rings' while the body says the general ramified case is open. Bhatt, Hochster and Ma (arXiv 24 Oct 2024; v2 25 Aug 2026; reported as Crelle vol. 835, 2026, not verified by me) prove equal-characteristic positivity via lim Cohen-Macaulay sequences and make mixed-characteristic positivity conditional on those sequences, which they do not establish for ramified rings. On 6 Oct 2026 OpenAI's openai/math release included 'Positivity of Serre's Intersection Multiplicity' (paper dated 23 Sep 2026, author line 'OpenAI'), which per the formal-conjectures issue and the unaoya README claims a full proof including the ramified mixed-characteristic case. I could not read the PDF: WebFetch returned compressed bytes, and the local PDF tool was not approved for this session, so its statement, hypotheses, method and any sentence about AI use are second-hand. The only authors' sentence about AI that I could quote is the repository README's statement that the manuscripts were 'produced by an internal OpenAI model', which covers the collection rather than this paper. No Lean proof of the paper exists upstream. The third-party Lean project has a statement skeleton with sorry-proved Theorem 1.1, and issue #6911 (7 Oct 2026) proposes marking the declarations solved, with no reply. No named commutative algebraist has written on the argument in the sources I could reach. Three other OpenAI manuscripts (Hodge-related) were withdrawn on 7 Oct for a sign error; coverage does not link any withdrawal to Serre positivity. I searched for other AI involvement (AlphaProof, GPT-5 and GPT-5.5 Pro, Claude, Aristotle, Lean/Mathlib formalisations, AI result trackers) and found no other AI-linked work on this problem. Close calls: (a) the OpenAI event is dated to 6 Oct 2026, the first public appearance I could find, not the 23 Sep 2026 date printed on the paper; (b) the equal-characteristic part of BHM may overlap pre-window results, see disputes; (c) the Wikipedia wording omits the finite-length hypothesis that the Lean version includes; (d) a search summary said Ishiro-Shimomoto (arXiv 2509.06527) restates the Serre conjecture under lim CM sequences, but the abstract page I opened does not mention it, so I record the abstract reading. Quotes from fetched pages were produced by a summarising fetcher with a short quote limit, so they are not byte-verified against the source.
competing_reading: The strongest reading that the OpenAI event settles the problem: the claim covers the full conjecture, including the ramified mixed-characteristic case that every source before it lists as the open one; the authors are a laboratory whose model has produced checked results in other cases; and an 'in full' claim with a stated scope would close the bullet if correct. The strongest reading against: nothing is verified yet (no Lean proof, no expert write-up after seven days, a skeleton-only formal project, OpenAI's own caution that unformalized results 'could have issues', and a withdrawal from the same batch), the scope and method are second-hand because I could not read the paper, and the one published route toward mixed-characteristic positivity (lim Cohen-Macaulay sequences) remains conditional. A middle reading treats the claim as unverified but relevant, so the problem is open for counting until the paper is checked; the judging pass should weigh that against the 2024 partial results, which do not reach the ramified case in general.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Read the preprint's theorem, hypotheses and proof structure, and check whether it uses any conditional input such as lim Cohen-Macaulay sequences; this needs the PDF or its extracted text. (2) A Lean 4 proof of the module-form theorem with no sorry (the unaoya project's first milestone, or one from OpenAI or the formal-conjectures community). (3) Written verification by named commutative algebraists, for example in a blog, a journal referee report, or an accepted paper. (4) A decision by the formal-conjectures maintainers on issue #6911 and any change to the research-open tags. (5) For BHM: the Crelle final version and whether its equal-characteristic statement is new relative to Serre's results. (6) For KC and Soto Levins: whether the quotient pair R/P, R/Q is Serre liftable in any case, and the final IMRN text.
